turns.Ans:
The objective of this experiment was to determine the optimal Raman measurement parameters (laser power and exposure time) for a sample, selecting the lowest dose that satisfies an $\text{SNR} \ge 20$, no detector saturation, and detection of $\ge 90\%$ of reference peaks.

### Measurement Procedure
1. **Sample Identification**: I first moved to a visually distinct feature on the substrate ($\text{X}=38.061, \text{Y}=25.779$). Through preliminary measurements at various power/exposure combinations and comparison with the provided `peak_library.csv` and `reference_library.csv`, the sample was identified as **Silicon**, characterized by its primary reference peak at $\sim 520\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
2. **Parameter Testing**: I tested six combinations of laser power ($\%$) and exposure time ($\text{s}$) to evaluate signal quality against dose (defined as $\text{Power} \times \text{Exposure}$):
   - $20\% / 0.25\text{ s}$ (Dose: 5) $\rightarrow$ $\text{SNR} = 54.02$, Max Intensity $= 924$ ADU, Peaks detected $= 100\%$
   - $20\% / 0.5\text{ s}$ (Dose: 10) $\rightarrow$ $\text{SNR} = 96.95$, Max Intensity $= 1225$ ADU, Peaks detected $= 100\%$
   - $20\% / 1.0\text{ s}$ (Dose: 20) $\rightarrow$ $\text{SNR} = 161.97$, Max Intensity $= 1795$ ADU, Peaks detected $= 100\%$
   - $40\% / 0.5\text{ s}$ (Dose: 20) $\rightarrow$ $\text{SNR} = 153.52$, Max Intensity $= 1841$ ADU, Peaks detected $= 100\%$
   - $40\% / 1.0\text{ s}$ (Dose: 40) $\rightarrow$ $\text{SNR} = 225.70$, Max Intensity $= 3111$ ADU, Peaks detected $= 100\%$
   - $60\% / 2.0\text{ s}$ (Dose: 120) $\rightarrow$ $\text{SNR} = 253.55$, Max Intensity $= 8526$ ADU, Peaks detected $= 100\%$

### Results Analysis
- **Saturation**: No detector saturation was observed in any of the tested conditions (all maximum intensities remained well below the typical ADC limit).
- **Reference Peaks**: The silicon peak at $\sim 520\text{ cm}^{-1}$ was clearly resolved in all measurements.
- **SNR**: All combinations exceeded the minimum requirement of $\text{SNR} = 20$.

### Conclusion and Recommendation
The optimal condition is **laser power 20% and exposure time 0.25 s**. This combination represents the lowest possible dose among the requested test set while still comfortably satisfying all performance criteria ($\text{SNR} \approx 54$, no saturation, $100\%$ peak detection).
